docs.title: 01 indiginious nations
docs.text: A detailed, high-quality historical cartographic map titled "Major Indigenous Civilizations Before 1492" in a 16:9 wide-landscape format, styled as an authoritative US history textbook illustration. MAP CONTENT — label and shade each of the following culture regions with distinct, harmonious colors: NORTHEAST: Haudenosaunee (Iroquois) Confederacy (Great Lakes / upstate New York), Algonquian peoples (Atlantic seaboard) SOUTHEAST: Mississippian culture centered on Cahokia (near modern St. Louis), Cherokee homeland (Appalachians), Choctaw / Chickasaw / Creek territories GREAT PLAINS: Lakota / Sioux, Comanche, Cheyenne, and Arapaho ranges; mark bison migration corridors with subtle dotted arrows SOUTHWEST: Ancestral Pueblo / Anasazi (Four Corners region), Hohokam (Sonoran Desert, Arizona), Mogollon, Navajo / Diné, Apache GREAT BASIN: Paiute, Shoshone, Ute territories NORTHWEST COAST: Chinook, Tlingit, Haida, Salish — mark coastal trade canoe routes with thin blue lines PLATEAU: Nez Perce, Yakama CALIFORNIA: Chumash, Ohlone, Yurok — note dense population concentration ARCTIC / SUBARCTIC: Inuit (Thule culture) along northern coastline, Athabascan interior MESOAMERICAN BORDER: indicate Aztec / Mexica empire to the south in muted tones (just northern tip visible) KEY SITES TO MARK WITH ICONS: - Cahokia Mounds (largest pre-Columbian city north of Mexico, ~20,000 pop.) - Chaco Canyon (Ancestral Pueblo ceremonial center) - Poverty Point, Louisiana (ancient mound complex) - Mesa Verde cliff dwellings - Serpent Mound, Ohio TRADE NETWORKS: overlay thin dashed lines showing the major inter-regional trade routes connecting these cultures (shell trade from Gulf Coast, obsidian from Rockies, copper from Great Lakes) CARTOGRAPHIC STYLE: - Parchment or aged cream background with subtle texture - Soft watercolor-style shading for regional territories with semi-transparent fills - Clean, readable serif labels in dark brown or black ink - Decorative compass rose (bottom right), scale bar (bottom left) - Small inset illustrations: a longhouse (Northeast), pueblo cliff dwelling (Southwest), totem pole (Northwest), earthen mound (Southeast) - Bold title "Major Indigenous Civilizations Before 1492" at the top center in a serif display font - Subtitle in smaller type: "North America — Approximate Cultural Regions" - Soft drop shadows on labels for legibility - Professional legend box (lower left) with color key for culture regions OVERALL FEEL: authoritative, respectful, richly detailed — suitable for an Advanced Placement or college-level US History textbook. Color palette: muted earth tones (terracotta, sage green, ochre, slate blue, warm brown) with white text labels outlined for contrast against the terrain base. Aspect ratio 16:9, 4K resolution, photorealistic cartographic illustration style.

docs.title: MicroSims
docs.text:
MicroSims are small, interactive educational simulations — each one focused on a single concept. They live under docs/sims/<sim-name>/ and are embedded into chapters via iframes.

New MicroSims can be created with the microsim-generator skill, which routes to the appropriate library (p5.js, Chart.js, vis-network, Mermaid, Leaflet, Plotly, Venn.js).

docs.title: Learning Graph Viewer
docs.text: This interactive viewer allows you to explore the learning graph for this course.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Search: Type in the search box to find specific concepts
  • Category Filtering: Use checkboxes to show/hide concept categories
  • Interactive Navigation: Click and drag to explore, scroll to zoom
  • Statistics: View real-time counts of visible nodes and edges

docs.title: Using the Viewer
docs.text:
1. Search for Concepts: Start typing in the search box to find concepts. Click on a result to focus on that node.

  2. Filter by Category: Use the category checkboxes in the sidebar to show or hide groups of related concepts. Use "Check All" or "Uncheck All" for bulk operations.

  3. Navigate the Graph:

  4. Drag to pan around the graph
  5. Scroll to zoom in and out

  6. Click on a node to select it and highlight its connections

  7. View Statistics: The sidebar shows counts of visible nodes, edges, and foundational concepts.

docs.title: Graph Structure
docs.text:
• Foundational Concepts (left side): Prerequisites with no dependencies
  • Advanced Concepts (right side): Topics that build on multiple prerequisites
  • Edges: Arrows point from a concept to its prerequisites
